items.title: NIST SP 800-63A - Identity proofing (IAL2)
items.text: Identity assurance level 2 requires evidence of real-world existence, validation of identity evidence against authoritative or issuing sources, and verification that the applicant is the genuine owner of the evidence (for example biometric comparison with presentation-attack detection) for remote or in-person proofing.

items.title: NIST SP 800-63B - Authentication (AAL2)
items.text: Authenticator assurance level 2 requires proof of possession and control of two distinct authentication factors, with reauthentication and session-timeout requirements and resistance to replay attacks.

items.title: ISO/IEC 30107-3 - Biometric presentation attack detection
items.text: Defines testing and reporting of presentation-attack detection mechanisms, including attack presentation classification error rate (APCER) and bona fide presentation classification error rate (BPCER).

items.title: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard 4.0
items.text: Provides verifiable security requirements for authentication, session management, access control, input validation, cryptography at rest, error handling and logging, data protection, communications security, file upload handling and API security.

items.title: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A controls
items.text: Annex A includes controls on access control and least privilege, segregation of duties, cryptography, logging and monitoring, secure development life cycle, supplier relationships and information-security incident management.

items.title: Org KYC & Customer Acceptance Policy v3.2
items.text: No account may be opened for anonymous or fictitious names or shell entities. Customers are rated low, medium or high risk using the approved risk-scoring model. High-risk and PEP relationships require EDD and approval by a senior compliance officer. Any manual override of a KYC decision requires maker-checker approval with a recorded reason.

items.title: Org Data Classification & Retention Standard v2.0
items.text: Identity documents, biometric templates and national identifiers are Restricted data: they must be encrypted at rest with AES-256 using HSM-managed keys and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher, masked in non-production environments and UIs by default, and retained per the regulatory retention schedule, then securely deleted.

items.title: Org Identity & Access Management Standard v4.1
items.text: All staff access to customer PII requires role-based access, MFA and quarterly access recertification. Privileged access is just-in-time and session-recorded. Customer sessions time out after 15 minutes of inactivity.

items.title: Org Responsible AI & Model Risk Policy v1.1
items.text: Models that influence customer decisions must be validated before use, monitored for drift and bias across protected groups, produce explainable outcomes, and keep a human in the loop for adverse decisions. LLM outputs must be grounded in approved sources and logged.

items.title: Org Service Level & Resilience Standard v1.4
items.text: Customer-facing tier-1 services target 99.9% monthly availability, RTO 4 hours and RPO 15 minutes, with active-passive disaster recovery tested twice a year and P1 incidents acknowledged within 15 minutes.
